Hmm, this looks pretty interesting. ChatGPT's latest update adds a new Mac integration: the ability to handle conversations from the Apple Messages app. The feature supports iMessage, SMS and RCS.

ChatGPT Mac 版新增 Apple Messages 插件

The new Apple Messages plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat history on Mac, as well as compose and send messages. OpenAI says the feature is now available across all tiers of the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, including ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This level of access raises privacy and control concerns, so OpenAI stresses that by default, sending messages still requires user approval. Users should think carefully before granting persistent approval. OpenAI's plugin guide details the relevant risks, how to revoke access, and a known issue involving tasks that skip approval prompts.

Separately, OpenAI detailed how the Messages feature works on its dedicated plugin site:

For now, the feature only works on Macs with Apple Silicon and is not supported on Intel models.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, it will pop up a confirmation prompt before sending. You can also choose to skip the confirmation step on a per-conversation basis.

Looking for this new feature in ChatGPT? This link will take you straight to the Messages plugin for ChatGPT on Mac.

Collaborative site editing, shared conversation snapshots and more

Although the Messages plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also brings a number of other improvements. For instance, pinned conversations will now stay in sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, letting users keep important chats within reach across Mac and iPhone.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots don't change when the original conversation is updated.

Links created from personal accounts can be accessed by anyone with the URL, while workspace links are restricted to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex redacts known sensitive formats, but reminds users to review snapshots because sensitive data may still slip through.

Beyond that, site owners can invite active members of the same workspace to collaboratively edit sites that support collaboration. Editors can update content and knowledge base data, save versions, and publish changes once the owner has handled the initial publish. Owners retain control over access, settings, analytics and version restore.

Some site owners can also change ChatGPT-hosted URLs without redeploying, with the old URL automatically redirecting to the new one.

Finally, the Computer History feature launched last week is being expanded to Pro, Business and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the UK. This opt-in feature requires the Memories feature to be enabled and is off by default.

You can see the full release announcement for this update here.
